title: World History: Year 1 to 2026
description: Important incidents and events organized by century

events.title: Birth of Christianity
events.description: Jesus crucified in Jerusalem, founding Christianity.

events.title: Eruption of Mount Vesuvius
events.description: Destroys Pompeii and Herculaneum.

events.title: Roman Empire greatest extent under Trajan
events.description: Maximum territorial expansion.

events.title: Spread of Buddhism to China
events.description: Buddhist missionaries arrive via Silk Road.

events.title: Invention of paper in China
events.description: Cai Lun refines papermaking.

events.title: Five Good Emperors of Rome
events.description: Golden age of Roman stability and prosperity.
events.source: Gibbon, Decline and Fall; Cassius Dio

events.title: Bar Kokhba Revolt
events.description: Jewish rebellion crushed, Judea renamed Syria Palaestina.

events.title: Hadrian's Wall constructed
events.description: 73-mile defensive wall across northern Britain.

events.title: Christianity spreads throughout Empire
events.description: Christian communities in every major city by 200 AD.

events.title: Han Dynasty begins collapse
events.description: Yellow Turban Rebellion leads to Three Kingdoms.

events.title: Crisis of the Third Century
events.description: Rome nearly collapses. Over 20 emperors in 50 years.

events.title: Three Kingdoms Period in China
events.description: China split into Wei, Shu, Wu.

events.title: Goths invade Roman Empire
events.description: Emperor Decius killed at Battle of Abritus.

events.title: Diocletian becomes Emperor
events.description: Establishes Tetrarchy, last great Christian persecution.

events.title: Maya Classic Period begins
events.description: Major Maya city-states rise.
events.source: Martin & Grube, Chronicle of the Maya Kings and Queens

events.title: Constantine converts to Christianity
events.description: Vision before Battle of Milvian Bridge. First Christian Roman Emperor.

events.title: Edict of Milan
events.description: Constantine legalizes Christianity, ending centuries of persecution.

events.title: Council of Nicaea
events.description: First ecumenical council, establishes Nicene Creed.

events.title: Founding of Constantinople
events.description: Capital moved from Rome to Byzantium. Center of Eastern civilization for 1000+ years.

events.title: Battle of Adrianople
events.description: Goths defeat Romans, Emperor Valens killed. Beginning of the end for Western Rome.

events.title: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
events.description: Odoacer deposes last emperor Romulus Augustulus. Ancient world ends, Middle Ages begin.

events.title: Attila the Hun invades Europe
events.description: Devastating campaigns, 'Scourge of God.' Stopped at Catalaunian Plains.

events.title: Sack of Rome by Visigoths
events.description: First sack of Rome in 800 years. Shocks the ancient world.
events.source: Augustine, City of God; Zosimus, New History

events.title: Northern and Southern Dynasties in China
events.description: Period of division and cultural flourishing, Buddhism spreads.

events.title: Anglo-Saxon settlement of Britain
events.description: Germanic tribes migrate after Roman withdrawal, shaping English identity.
events.source: Bede, Ecclesiastical History of the English People

events.title: Justinian's Code published
events.description: Codifies Roman law into Corpus Juris Civilis, foundation of Western legal systems.

events.title: Plague of Justinian
events.description: Bubonic plague kills 25-50 million, 13-26% of world population.

events.title: Birth of Prophet Muhammad
events.description: Founder of Islam born in Mecca. Transforms Middle East and beyond.

events.title: Hagia Sophia constructed
events.description: World's largest cathedral for nearly 1000 years. Architectural marvel.

events.title: Sui Dynasty reunifies China
events.description: Reunites northern and southern China after centuries of division.

events.title: Rise of Islam and Muslim conquests
events.description: Muhammad flees Mecca to Medina (Hijra, 622). Within a century, Islamic empire stretches from Spain to India.
events.source: Ibn Ishaq, Sirat Rasul Allah; Al-Tabari, Tarikh

events.title: Tang Dynasty begins in China
events.description: China's golden age of culture, poetry, trade. Capital Chang'an becomes world's largest city.

events.title: Battle of Tours
events.description: Charles Martel defeats Umayyad Caliphate, halting Muslim expansion into Western Europe.

events.title: Viking Age begins
events.description: Raid on Lindisfarne monastery. Norse expansion reshapes Europe.
events.source: Anglo-Saxon Chronicle; Alcuin of York letters

events.title: Feudalism emerges in Europe
events.description: After Rome's fall, feudal system becomes dominant political and economic structure.

events.title: Battle of Talas
events.description: Abbasid Caliphate defeats Tang China. Papermaking transfers to Islamic world.

events.title: Charlemagne crowned Holy Roman Emperor
events.description: Unites much of Western Europe for first time since Rome.

events.title: Islamic Golden Age begins
events.description: Baghdad becomes center of science, philosophy, medicine. House of Wisdom established.

events.title: Nara Period in Japan
events.description: First permanent capital. Buddhism becomes state religion.

events.title: Borobudur temple constructed
events.description: World's largest Buddhist temple in Java.

events.title: Vikings discover Iceland
events.description: Norse explorers settle Iceland, later reaching Greenland and North America.

events.title: East-West Christian Schism begins
events.description: Growing divide between Roman Catholic and Eastern Orthodox churches.
events.source: Photios I, Mystagogy of the Holy Spirit

events.title: An Lushan Rebellion
events.description: Devastating Tang civil war, 13-36 million deaths. Tang never fully recovers.

events.title: Gunpowder invented in China
events.description: Chinese alchemists discover gunpowder. Transforms warfare globally.

events.title: Foundation of Kievan Rus
events.description: Oleg of Novgorod unites Eastern Slavic tribes, precursor to Russia.

events.title: Song Dynasty begins in China
events.description: Extraordinary innovation: movable type, compass, gunpowder weapons, paper money.

events.title: Leif Erikson reaches North America
events.description: First European in the Americas, 500 years before Columbus.
events.source: Saga of the Greenlanders; Saga of Erik the Red

events.title: Holy Roman Empire established
events.description: Otto I crowned Emperor. Lasts until 1806.

events.title: Great Zimbabwe constructed
events.description: Capital of Kingdom of Zimbabwe, center of gold and ivory trade.

events.title: Islamic Golden Age at peak
events.description: Alhazen (optics), Avicenna (medicine), Al-Biruni (astronomy).
events.source: Ibn al-Haytham, Book of Optics; Ibn Sina, Canon of Medicine

events.title: Great Schism of 1054
events.description: Eastern Orthodox and Roman Catholic churches formally split, dividing Christianity permanently.
events.source: Michael Cerularius correspondence; Humbert of Silva Candida's bull of excommunication

events.title: Norman Conquest of England
events.description: William the Conqueror defeats King Harold at Hastings. Reshapes English language, culture, governance.

events.title: First Crusade
events.description: European Christians capture Jerusalem, establishing Crusader States in the Middle East.
events.source: Fulcher of Chartres, Chronicle; Anna Komnene, Alexiad

events.title: Seljuk Turks defeat Byzantines at Manzikert
events.description: Opens Anatolia to Turkish settlement, leads to Crusades.

events.title: Movable type printing in China
events.description: Bi Sheng creates world's first movable type printing system, centuries before Gutenberg.
events.source: Shen Kuo, Dream Pool Essays (Mengxi Bitan)

events.title: Genghis Khan born
events.description: Founder of the Mongol Empire, the largest contiguous land empire in history.
events.source: The Secret History of the Mongols

events.title: Third Crusade
events.description: Richard the Lionheart, Saladin, and Frederick Barbarossa clash over Jerusalem. Saladin retains the city.
events.source: Ibn al-Athir, al-Kamil fi al-Tarikh; Roger of Hoveden, Chronica

events.title: Song Dynasty innovation peak
events.description: Compass, gunpowder weapons, paper money, canal lock gates. China leads the world in technology.
events.source: History of Song (Songshi); Joseph Needham, Science and Civilisation in China

events.title: Angkor Wat constructed
events.description: Largest religious monument ever built, in present-day Cambodia.

events.title: Universities of Bologna and Oxford founded
events.description: Birth of the European university system.
events.source: University archives; Rashdall, The Universities of Europe in the Middle Ages

events.title: Mongol Empire expands rapidly
events.description: Genghis Khan unites Mongol tribes (1206). Largest contiguous empire ever, from Korea to Hungary.
events.source: The Secret History of the Mongols; Rashid al-Din, Jami al-Tawarikh

events.title: Magna Carta signed
events.description: King John forced to sign, limiting royal power. Foundation of constitutional law and individual rights.
events.source: British Library, original Magna Carta manuscript

events.title: Mongols sack Baghdad
events.description: Destroy the Abbasid Caliphate. End of the Islamic Golden Age. Millions killed.
events.source: The Secret History of the Mongols; Ibn al-Athir

events.title: Marco Polo travels to China
events.description: Venetian merchant documents Silk Road journey, introducing Europe to Asian civilization.
events.source: Marco Polo, The Travels of Marco Polo (Il Milione)

events.title: First handgun developed in China
events.description: Earliest known firearm, the Heilongjiang hand cannon.

events.title: The Black Death
events.description: Bubonic plague kills 75-200 million, 30-60% of Europe's population. Most devastating pandemic in recorded history.
events.source: Giovanni Boccaccio, The Decameron; Ibn Khaldun, Muqaddimah

events.title: Hundred Years' War begins
events.description: England and France wage prolonged conflict. Joan of Arc leads French forces. Shapes both nations.

events.title: Ottoman Empire founded
events.description: Osman I establishes the Ottoman Beylik. Will become one of history's greatest empires.

events.title: Ming Dynasty founded in China
events.description: Zhu Yuanzhang drives out the Mongols. Ming era sees construction of the Forbidden City.

events.title: Renaissance begins in Italy
events.description: Cultural rebirth in Florence and other city-states. Rediscovery of classical learning transforms art and science.
events.source: Giorgio Vasari, Lives of the Most Excellent Painters, Sculptors, and Architects

events.title: Fall of Constantinople
events.description: Ottoman Sultan Mehmed II conquers Constantinople. End of the Byzantine Empire after 1,100 years.
events.source: Laonikos Chalkokondyles, Histories; Kritovoulos, History of Mehmed the Conqueror

events.title: Gutenberg's printing press
events.description: Johannes Gutenberg invents movable type printing in Europe. Revolutionizes knowledge dissemination.

events.title: Columbus reaches the Americas
events.description: Christopher Columbus lands in the Bahamas. Begins the Age of Exploration and European colonization.
events.source: Christopher Columbus, Journal of the First Voyage

events.title: Vasco da Gama reaches India
events.description: First European to reach India by sea. Opens direct trade route between Europe and Asia.

events.title: Leonardo da Vinci paints the Last Supper
events.description: Epitome of Renaissance genius. Da Vinci also designs flying machines, tanks, and anatomical studies.
events.source: Giorgio Vasari, Lives of the Artists

events.title: Protestant Reformation
events.description: Martin Luther posts 95 Theses (1517). Splits Western Christianity, triggering wars and reshaping Europe.
events.source: Martin Luther, 95 Theses; Philip Schaff, History of the Christian Church

events.title: Spanish conquest of the Aztec and Inca Empires
events.description: Cortés conquers the Aztecs (1521). Pizarro conquers the Incas (1533). Millions of indigenous people die from disease and war.
events.source: Bernal Díaz del Castillo, True History of the Conquest of New Spain

events.title: Copernicus proposes heliocentric model
events.description: On the Revolutions of the Celestial Spheres (1543). Revolutionizes astronomy and scientific thought.
events.source: Nicolaus Copernicus, De Revolutionibus Orbium Coelestium

events.title: Ottoman Empire reaches peak under Suleiman the Magnificent
events.description: Ottoman Empire at its height, dominating the Mediterranean, Middle East, and Southeast Europe.

events.title: Shakespeare writes his plays
events.description: William Shakespeare produces the greatest body of literature in the English language.

events.title: Galileo's astronomical discoveries
events.description: Telescope observations confirm Copernican model. Catholic Church forces him to recant.
events.source: Galileo Galilei, Sidereus Nuncius; Dialogue Concerning the Two Chief World Systems

events.title: Thirty Years' War
events.description: Devastating religious conflict in Europe. Peace of Westphalia (1648) establishes modern state system.
events.source: Peace of Westphalia treaties; C.V. Wedgwood, The Thirty Years War

events.title: Newton publishes Principia Mathematica
events.description: Isaac Newton's laws of motion and universal gravitation. Foundation of classical physics.
events.source: Isaac Newton, Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica

events.title: Qing Dynasty begins in China
events.description: Manchus overthrow the Ming Dynasty. Qing will be China's last imperial dynasty.

events.title: Dutch East India Company founded
events.description: First multinational corporation and the first to issue stock. Dominates global spice trade.

events.title: Industrial Revolution begins
events.description: Steam engine, mechanized factories transform Britain then the world. Shift from agrarian to industrial society.
events.source: Arnold Toynbee, Lectures on the Industrial Revolution; E.P. Thompson, The Making of the English Working Class

events.title: American Revolution and Independence
events.description: 13 colonies declare independence (1776). Creates the first modern democratic republic.
events.source: Declaration of Independence; Thomas Paine, Common Sense

events.title: French Revolution
events.description: Overthrow of the monarchy. Declaration of the Rights of Man. Reign of Terror. Napoleon rises.
events.source: Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen; Thomas Carlyle, The French Revolution

events.title: Adam Smith publishes The Wealth of Nations
events.description: Foundation of modern economics. Introduces concepts of free markets and division of labor.
events.source: Adam Smith, An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations

events.title: James Watt improves the steam engine
events.description: Watt's efficient steam engine (1769) powers the Industrial Revolution.
events.source: James Watt patent records; Samuel Smiles, Lives of the Engineers

events.title: Napoleonic Wars
events.description: Napoleon conquers much of Europe. Defeated at Waterloo (1815). Reshapes European borders and nationalism.
events.source: David Chandler, The Campaigns of Napoleon

events.title: Darwin publishes On the Origin of Species
events.description: Theory of evolution by natural selection. Revolutionizes biology and challenges religious doctrine.
events.source: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species

events.title: American Civil War
events.description: Union defeats Confederacy. Slavery abolished. 600,000+ dead. Deadliest American conflict.
events.source: Shelby Foote, The Civil War; Emancipation Proclamation

events.title: Meiji Restoration in Japan
events.description: Japan modernizes and industrializes rapidly, transforming from feudal state to world power.
events.source: Meiji Constitution; Marius Jansen, The Making of Modern Japan

events.title: Scramble for Africa
events.description: European powers colonize nearly the entire African continent. Devastating consequences that last to this day.
events.source: Thomas Pakenham, The Scramble for Africa

events.title: World War I
events.description: 20 million dead. Destroys four empires (Ottoman, Austro-Hungarian, Russian, German). Reshapes the world map.
events.source: Barbara Tuchman, The Guns of August; Erich Maria Remarque, All Quiet on the Western Front

events.title: World War II
events.description: 70-85 million dead. Holocaust kills 6 million Jews. Atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki. Deadliest conflict in history.
events.source: Antony Beevor, The Second World War; Winston Churchill, The Second World War

events.title: Moon landing
events.description: Apollo 11. Neil Armstrong becomes first human to walk on the Moon.

events.title: Fall of the Berlin Wall
events.description: Cold War ends. Soviet Union dissolves (1991). Communism collapses across Eastern Europe.

events.title: Invention of the Internet
events.description: ARPANET (1969) to World Wide Web (1991, Tim Berners-Lee). Transforms communication, commerce, and society.
events.source: Tim Berners-Lee, Weaving the Web; Vinton Cerf and Bob Kahn, TCP/IP papers

events.title: September 11 attacks
events.description: Terrorist attacks on the World Trade Center and Pentagon kill nearly 3,000. Launches the War on Terror.

events.title: iPhone released
events.description: Apple's iPhone launches the smartphone era. By 2026, smartphones are used by 5+ billion people.

events.title: COVID-19 pandemic
events.description: SARS-CoV-2 kills an estimated 20+ million worldwide. Lockdowns, remote work, mRNA vaccines.
events.source: WHO pandemic reports; Johns Hopkins COVID dashboard

events.title: Rise of AI and large language models
events.description: ChatGPT launches (Nov 2022), followed by GPT-4, Claude, Gemini. AI transforms work, education, creative industries.

events.title: Russia invades Ukraine
events.description: Largest military conflict in Europe since WWII. Reshapes global alliances, energy markets, and geopolitics.
events.source: Various international news agencies; UN resolutions

events.title: Israel-Palestine conflict escalates — Gaza genocide
events.description: Following October 7, 2023 Hamas attack, Israel launches massive military campaign in Gaza. Tens of thousands of Palestinian civilians killed. ICJ investigates.
events.source: UN Human Rights Council reports; ICJ provisional measures order (2024); Amnesty International; Human Rights Watch

events.title: Israel strikes Iran
events.description: Israel launches direct military strikes against Iranian targets, escalating regional conflict across the Middle East.
events.source: Various international news agencies; Reuters; AP
